opportunity: foldcallret proves a single-use call output order-safe to fold, but ActionMarkImplied re-tests it in check_implied_cover, whose Merge::inflate_test arm forces it explicit when an operand has another live SSA version of the same HighVariable over the call output's cover. Upstream never reaches that arm with a call output, and the version it collides with is the CPUI_INDIRECT the call itself attaches to a global it reads as an argument, so passing stdin/stdout/errno to a call is enough to block the fold.
test_name: tests/stages/kuna-foldcallretphi.xml (default passes first, no option command: helper undeclared = the spill kept by the width guard; helper declared int4 = the fold; target2 = a global write in the span keeps the spill; target3 = gcc -O2 setcc/and for (r == 0) && (a > 5), the call's value the right operand of BOOL_AND = the spill kept; then option foldcallretphi off = the spills) + tests/stages/kuna-foldcallretphi-join.xml (i386 edx:eax: undeclared big keeps the spill, declared int4 folds, off keeps it) + 3 option-parse unit tests + the architecture default assertion
binary: synthetic bytechunk (x86:LE:64:default:gcc) in the stage test
inspiration: angr call-return variable folding (the fold angr performs unconditionally where kuna's second gate declines); foldcallret
root_cause: check_implied_cover's inflate_test arm was written for ordinary expressions and only sees call outputs because of kuna's foldcallret escape. The collision it reports is produced by the call being folded: a call may write any global, so it carries a CPUI_INDIRECT over every global it touches, and that INDIRECT's output is another instance of the argument's own HighVariable, live from the call onwards.
hypothesis_refuted: The E2 report's ceiling hypothesis (ActionMergeRequired runs before ActionMarkExplicit, so a force-merged call output fails num_instances()>1) is not what blocks the named witnesses: every one of them reports ninst=1 at base_explicit. num_instances()>1 does veto 141 other call outputs across the six sweep binaries, but those highs have 2-22 members from speculative datatype merges, not the single trim COPY a relaxation would need, so that ceiling is documented and left standing.

corpus_sweep.foldmove: 1270 removed call spills located; 718 mapped to their landing statement -- 711 land on the very next statement, 7 with one intervening statement (a register or constant assignment), and none crosses a call, a memory access or a control-flow boundary. default_on_ablation.why_held_off: `--assert type vN` / `--assert name vN` address a variable by its auto-generated name. Folding `v1 = strcmp(pass,sneaky)` into its `if` removes a declaration and renumbers the rest, so the probe's `type v2 char[16]` retypes a different stack slot (credbuf lands at -0x10 instead of -0x18 and a separate `char v2 [8]` appears). Neither listing is unsound; the directive simply no longer names what the user meant. The flip is therefore a change about --assert ergonomics rather than about this pass, and belongs in its own PR with those directives re-read.

print_point_guard.defect: The first version of the discount fired whenever the call's single use was order-safe, but `call_output_foldable` only guards the span up to that use. When the use op's own output is implied, the expression is printed wherever that implied value is finally consumed -- possibly a later block behind a branch -- and the inflate_test rejection the discount waives was the only thing holding the call in place.
print_point_guard.witness: betaflight_STM32F405.elf (O2, stripped) sub_8051ac4 @0x8051ac4: `sub_80515b4(dat_200181a4)` was emitted after `if (dat_200019cc & 1)`, while the binary calls at 0x8051b00 and first reads 0x200019cc at 0x8051b0e.
print_point_guard.fix: print_point() follows the implied chain from the use op to the statement the folded expression actually lands in, and print_point_is_order_safe() re-runs foldcallret's span guard (same block, strictly after, no CALL/LOAD/STORE/CALLOTHER and no read of an INDIRECT the call writes) over that whole distance.
print_point_guard.verification: An env-gated throwaway build (KUNA_FCRPHI_NOGUARD, reverted) reproduces the hunk exactly; with the guard the function is byte-identical to `--option foldcallretphi off`. The fmt witnesses still fold (`v11 &= sub_3700(stdin,v6);`, `if (sub_41f0(stdin))`).

related_issue: Noelo-Lab/kuna#657 -- the pre-existing default-on foldcallret gap: a heritage-promoted global assignment is a CPUI_COPY, so op_is_barrier lets a call sink past a write to a global the callee reads. Independent of this option (same output with it on or off).

tied_write_guard.defect: op_is_barrier tests opcodes (CALL/LOAD/STORE/CALLOTHER), but heritage promotes a write to a fixed address into a plain CPUI_COPY, so a fold could cross one. With --option foldcallretphi on, `v2 = helper(g); k = 42; ok = v1 & v2;` became `ok = v1 & helper(g);` -- the call evaluated after the write to k that it reads. origin/main and --option foldcallretphi off emit the correct order.
tied_write_guard.witness: synthetic x86-64 asm (target/helper/k/g/ok), reproduced verbatim from the round-3 review; compiling both renderings gives ok=1 (off, matching the binary) against ok=42 (on, before the fix)
tied_write_guard.fix: op_writes_tied_storage declines any op between the call and the print point whose output varnode is persistent or address-tied; the guard runs over the whole travel distance, which contains foldcallret's call-to-use span, so every fold the discount adds is covered. Marker ops are skipped (an INDIRECT records a write its effect op performs). The frame half is not optional: print raw on a function that passes &loc to a callee and then writes loc shows the escaped slot promoted exactly like a global (s0xffffffffffffffe0:4 = #0x2a:4, a CPUI_COPY), so the earlier argument that an escaped slot stays a CPUI_STORE was wrong.
tied_write_guard.verification: built without the barrier and otherwise identical: the counterexample folds again and stage assertion #5 fails; with it, on == off == origin/main. Re-swept over the 24 binaries with the full barrier: all three metrics report identical numbers (1270 located, 718 mapped, 0 hazards, 9 event-set + 40 event-order diffs), so it costs no folds, and five binaries change in one shape each -- a local assignment that had moved across a strlen call goes back to its off-arm position (du, diff x2, find, grep, tar). A write to a local is not an event for either metric, so those six reorders were in no hazard count; the barrier removes them structurally.
tied_write_guard.print_point_indirect_test: op_reads_indirect_output_of is now applied to the statement the expression lands in as well as to the single use op -- with an implied chain longer than one hop those are different ops. It declines 5 folds on the sweep (O0/O2 grep main, O0 grep sub_828e, cleanflight sub_8017f4c, crazyflie sub_8009c74), each one a landing statement that reads a global or a frame slot the call carries an INDIRECT over.
tied_write_guard.sibling: Noelo-Lab/kuna#657 -- the same hole through default-on foldcallret alone, fixed separately because it moves default output.

width_guard.what: conflict_is_self_call_effect declines unless the call's output carries the callee's whole return value: a locked output, or an unlocked one as wide as the prototype model's return entry holding it (call_output_is_full_width; ProtoModel::output_entries). An unlocked eax read out of rax keeps its spill.
width_guard.why: sort O2 main: int v15 = sub_c5b0(stdin); v15 == -1 folded to sub_c5b0(stdin) == -1, and kuna prints sub_c5b0 (rpl_fclose, binary mov $0xffffffff,%eax) as unsigned long ... return 0xffffffff; -- the compare is never true. Before the guard: 9 such new always-false -1 checks over 32 binaries, ~44/45 narrowing drops per sweep set.
width_guard.after: narrowcount.py over 32 binaries: lost 0; uncast f(..) == -1 on an 8-byte callee 45 off -> 46 default, the one extra being du O0 sub_11107 getline(..) != -1 whose spill was long (correct)
width_guard.remaining_cost: same-width signedness of an unlocked full-width output; over 32 binaries no folded undeclared call feeds a relational compare, shift or division (all 32 relational uses are declared libc calls or print a cast)

joined_pairs.what: call_output_is_full_width also asks the model where it would return an int of each power-of-two size above the output's, up to long long (wider_int_return_contains, via ParamListStandard::assign_map on ProtoModel::output_list), and declines when that storage contains the output: i386 edx:eax (a join entry for 5..8 bytes the entry filter skipped) and ARM r0:r1 (a model rule, not an entry). Pairs wider than long long (rdx:rax, x0:x1) are not asked about.
joined_pairs.why: gcc -m32 -O2: int r = (int)big(g); if (r == -1) return 1; return 7; with big returning 0xffffffffLL printed as unsigned long long folded to if (big(g) != -1) return 7;, returning 7 where the binary returns 1
joined_pairs.effect: x86-64 unchanged (an 8-byte rax has no wider size to ask; narrower outputs were already declined); on 32-bit targets only declared callees fold: 53 ARM functions go back to the off text
